title: Barabbas (Mark 15:1–15)
hook: the crowd chooses a rebel over Jesus

segments.voice: Yesterday, a rooster crowed twice in a courtyard, and your line was he wept. Did you let an old failure be honestly sad for a moment? Day two hundred twenty-five.

Think of the last time you watched a pile-on. A comment section, a group chat, a hallway. One person says something, a few more join in, and within minutes a whole crowd is certain. Nobody quite remembers how it started, and nobody wants to be the one who says, wait. Early in the morning, the council binds Jesus and hands him over to Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor, because only Rome can carry out an execution. Pilate asks him: are you the King of the Jews? Jesus answers, thou sayest it, and then goes silent again, and Pilate marvels. Outside, a crowd is gathering.
screen: `A PILE-ON.` → `HANDED OVER TO PILATE.` → `A CROWD GATHERS.`

segments.voice: Mark says that at the feast, the governor used to release one prisoner, whoever the people asked for. It's worth saying plainly: no record outside the Gospels mentions this custom, and historians aren't sure how it worked. In prison there's a man called Barabbas, held with rebels who had committed murder in an uprising. Pilate asks the crowd: will you have me release the King of the Jews? Mark adds that Pilate knew the chief priests had handed Jesus over out of envy. And then, Mark says, the chief priests stir up the crowd to ask for Barabbas instead. Now a detail in the name. Barabbas is an Aramaic name: bar abba, son of the father. Remember abba, from the garden, four days ago? Jesus called God abba. Now the crowd is offered two men: one called son of the father, and one Christians call the Son of the Father. And some old copies of Matthew's Gospel even give the rebel's first name as Jesus. So Pilate asks, what then shall I do with him? Crucify him, they shout. Why, what evil hath he done? They shout louder. And Mark says, in the King James Bible: "And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified." Willing to content the people. The most powerful man in the province does what the loudest voices want. The crowd was a crowd that morning, stirred up by a few, and it was wrong. And many Christians see one more thing in this scene: the guilty man walks free, and the innocent one takes his place.
screen: `ONE PRISONER RELEASED AT THE FEAST.` · `BAR ABBA: SON OF THE FATHER.` · `CRUCIFY HIM.` · `WILLING TO CONTENT THE PEOPLE.` · then, large: `RELEASED BARABBAS UNTO THEM.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold in mind the crowds who get it wrong. Settle, and breathe. Think of a crowd you've seen lately turn on someone: online, at work, in the news. Picture the people in it, one by one, just ordinary people caught up in the noise. And picture the one they're shouting at. If you pray, you can pray for both: for the crowd, and for the person in the middle. If you don't, simply wish them all a quieter heart. The bell holds the time.
Barabbas. Bar abba, son of the father: the rebel the crowd chose to set free instead of Jesus.

Your line: the crowd isn't always right. Today, when you feel a crowd pulling you toward certainty about someone, be the one who pauses and asks, wait, what did he actually do? Day two hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: On Palm Sunday and Good Friday many churches read the passion aloud with the congregation speaking the crowd's lines, so that everyone says crucify him and remembers that the crowd's failure can be anyone's.

fork.setup: you're Pilate. you know the priests handed him over out of envy. the crowd is shouting crucify him. what do you do?
options: release Barabbas and hand Jesus over.
fork.reveal: Mark says Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas and delivered Jesus to be crucified.

trapdoor: what you thought: Barabbas was just a random criminal.
what it means: a rebel named son of the father goes free, and Jesus, who called God abba, is handed over.
what a scholar hears: bar abba is Aramaic, and some old manuscripts of Matthew 27:16–17 call him Jesus Barabbas.

sources.quoted: And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.

notes: 'Only Rome can carry out an execution' reflects John 18:31 and the usual historical view; confirm phrasing.
The Passover release custom (privilegium paschale) is attested only in the Gospels; confirm.
Some manuscripts of Matthew 27:16–17 read 'Jesus Barabbas' (e.g. Caesarean witnesses; Origen knew it). Confirm.
'Thou sayest it' (Mark 15:2) is KJV but given as a snippet within the voice, not cited as a separate quotation.

The substitution reading (the guilty freed, the innocent in his place) is attributed to Christian reflection, not to Mark's text. Care taken that the crowd is 'a crowd that morning, stirred up by a few', not a whole people.

Audit (wider sample): 'abba, from the garden, two days ago' corrected to four days ago (abba was day 221); cut the hype line 'the detail that stops scholars in their tracks' and the stock phrase 'Christians have long heard'.
